rationale: flops-3 is a tiny, float-arithmetic-bound kernel with a hot numeric loop and essentially no function-count or global-variable surface (n_functions null, no source lines, no large functions), so obfuscation value must come from the arithmetic/control-flow layer rather than call- or global-layer transforms. SUB is favored maximally: instruction substitution blends naturally into dense FP/integer arithmetic, is nearly free at runtime and size, and carries minimal correctness risk even under aggressive FP reassociation constraints. SPLIT is similarly cheap and adds basic-block diversity with negligible cost, so it is enabled with moderate security weight. FLA (control-flow flattening) provides the strongest structural resistance for a small function and is kept at moderate weight since its dispatch-loop overhead is tolerable in a short kernel but not free. BCF is strongly suppressed (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights) because bogus-control-flow bloat and slow the hot loop substantially while adding redundant opaque-predicate logic that a small benchmark does not need. IBR stays at moderate weights for indirect-branch diversity, while ICALL and IGV are weighted low across the board and biased toward their risk/cost dimensions since this program has almost no indirect calls or globals to hide, making their transformation overhead and linking-correctness risk unjustifiable.
